dialogues.speaker: Malevich
dialogues.text: Oh no... The Master had only used three blocks of Prime Ice for his work. But for me to create more or less the same form, I'll need five...

dialogues.speaker: Malevich
dialogues.text: *Sigh* If only someone could help me think of a way out...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "The Master"?

dialogues.speaker: Malevich
dialogues.text: #Yes, The Master. Oh... Hello, dear {M#sir}{F#madame}. Oh... hello to you to, flying miss.

dialogues.speaker: Malevich
dialogues.text: Has either of you... heard of the artist Kazimir Larionov by any chance? The one they call "The Master"?

choices.text: Nope.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Oh. The two of you... don't look like you're from Svetloledovka. So you might not have heard of an artist from around here. That's understandable. Yes, very understandable.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: He is a renowned master artist who's been hailed as "the master who ushered in a new age of Snezhnayan avant-garde art," "the father of Prime Ice aesthetics," and "the sole representative of the Glaciafruit school of art."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you say "Glaciafruit"? You mean his work is edible or something? Yum!

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Oh no, no, no, my dear flying miss. Hmm... how would the high-class folks in Snezhnograd put it...? Oh! They call that an "aesthetic."

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Most importantly, he grew up here, right in Svetloledovka! It's such an honor to be from the same town as our avant-garde master...

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: As the story goes, The Master had rather humble beginnings here. His family wasn't very wealthy, and he didn't go to school much either. In his younger days, he worked here in town as a laborer, at the ice quarry... which is also pretty much what I do now.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: But then, he went somewhere further in life. He created some beautiful sculptures out of Prime Ice, and later... his talent was discovered and he became an artist. That's when he left Svetloledovka to live among the high-class folks in Snezhnograd...

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: #I like this story very much, my dear {M#sir}{F#madame}, my dear flying miss, so much so that I, Malevich, decided to go into this line because of it...

choices.text: Do you wish to become an artist too?

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: #You are absolutely right, my dear {M#sir}{F#madame}. I wish to become an artist just like The Master.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Although I'm just an ordinary Prime Ice designer right now and have yet to make it out of Svetloledovka... At the very least, I can say that I'm starting off at the very same place as The Master.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: As long as I work hard to learn from The Master's ways and recreate his style, I will be able to walk the same path he did... all the way to Snezhnograd where I will be a great artist respected by all.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Then, I'll be able to stay in a big house and not have to worry about where my heating will come from. Who knows, I might even get to meet the Tsaritsa herself... and drink all the kvass I want without having to pay for it. No one will dare look down on me...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But you seem rather troubled right now.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: #*Sigh* you are right, my dear {M#sir}{F#madame}. I was presented with an opportunity that has however left me unsure of what to do.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: As luck would have it, the Prime Ice Art Exhibition happening soon in Snezhnograd is planning a special themed exhibition called "Classics, Redux: The Glaciafruit Master Returns (A Special Homage Exhibition)."

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: And the job orders for this exhibition are sent here to Svetloledovka... Since I've been imitating The Master all this while, you must see how important this opportunity is to me.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: #If I can faithfully reproduce The Master's work, my dear {M#sir}{F#madame}, maybe the artists in Snezhnograd will notice me...

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: But the order I received... *Sigh* The Master had used only three blocks of Prime Ice to create the original work. But for me to reproduce the work in the illustration, I'll need at least five.

choices.text: Must you stick to three blocks though?

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Of course, of course. The Master was able to use just three blocks of Prime Ice probably due to some ingenuity on his part. And that very ingenuity might just be why he's regarded as an artist.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: If I were to use five blocks of Prime Ice... whatever I end up making won't be The Master's work at all. And if I can't even recreate The Master's work, how am I supposed to walk the same path he did?

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Besides, the order only pays enough for three blocks of Prime Ice. I'll have to pay for any additional blocks used out of my own pocket...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's what this is really all about! The money!

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Th—— My dear flying miss, I don't think it's very fair of you to say that. While it is also important that I am paid my due, I wouldn't be so vexed if this was only about a few Mora.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: What I'm really worried about is... what would the folks in Snezhnograd think if I can't come up with a faithful reproduction of The Master's work? I can't afford to let this precious opportunity go to waste.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Just to prove to the both of you... that I, Malevich, am not as small-minded as you think, I'm willing to give you the payment for this order, as long as the two of you can help me think of a way out.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's take a look at that job order first.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Here's the job order... look at the illustration over here. We'll have to remove two blocks of Prime Ice somehow. And if you succeed, you can have the payment for the job order.

choices.text: Maybe just completing the work would be a victory in itself.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Oh, it's really nice of you to say that to make me feel better. But... what if he's regarded as an artist precisely because he's able to make it out of three blocks of Prime Ice?

choices.text: Do you wish to become one of the "high-class folks" too?

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: #Oh... I have never thought of it that way, my dear {M#sir}{F#madame}.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: I just wish to become an artist just like The Master.

choices.text: He must be really famous, then?

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Of course, of course! Oh. The two of you... don't look like you're from Svetloledovka. So you might not have heard of an artist from around here. That's understandable. Yes, very understandable.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: He's been hailed as "the master who ushered in a new age of Snezhnayan avant-garde art," "the father of Prime Ice aesthetics," and "the sole representative of the Glaciafruit school of art."

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: Those Art Exhibition jobs are always such a headache. If there's one thing they're good at, it's turning a simple matter into a whole problem.

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: If anyone can just take care of this job for me, I'm more than happy to give them all the career honors I've received over the years.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: Are you talking to me? As you can see, I am currently suffering through this pitifully paid job dressed up as "art."

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: I have here a job from the people at The Master exhibition in Snezhnograd. You can never say no to these Snezhnograd jobs, even though they're always technically demanding and pay very little for the trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: If I were to say no, they'd say, "Oh, but Zarkaya, this is a work that only an artist-tier designer like you can take on! We can't trust anyone else with it!"

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: "Artist"? After all these years, I finally understand that Prime Ice sculpting is nothing more than a job. So I'd rather they treat me as just another ordinary designer. And you know why?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: Because in the time I spend merely working out the structure of a "work of art" like this, I can easily finish five ordinary "non-art" jobs that pay exactly the same. Each.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That does sound like a bad deal for you!

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: That's right. So whenever I get a job like this, a saying popular among us Prime Ice designers comes to mind: "Art or a full belly, that is the question."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I suppose Paimon would go for "a full belly."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I suppose "art" isn't a bad choice either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not at all! But first, we'll have to find someplace where we can make ourselves enough Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: Oh? In that case, I have a proposal that may interest you...

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: If the two of you can help me position the next block of Prime Ice, I'll gladly share half the payment for this job with you — and even relinquish to you the title of "Artist-Tier Designer."

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: That is to say, if the two of you are willing to spend some time helping me complete this job in the name of "art," I will provide you with material compensation in addition to the immense psychological satisfaction you will undoubtedly gain.

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: As for me, I'll be free to take on other jobs with the time you save me, and thus fill my belly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wow, {NICKNAME}! Paimon thinks she said "material compensation"...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We do have a little expertise when it comes to "art," yes.

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: Wonderful. Then you are absolutely the right people for the job.

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: According to the job specifications, we'll have to place another block of Prime Ice on top. You may want to take a look at the illustration first before you get started.

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: "The Master," they say? Ha! It seems their taste over in Snezhnograd is truly in decline. Not one of the works in this job can be said to possess even the slightest compositional discipline.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Compositional discipline"...?

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: That's right, compositional discipline. And that is the ultimate Prime Ice aesthetic standard that our years of practice have bestowed upon our generation, upon our Snezhnaya.

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: I still remember those days when I was in art school in Snezhnograd. Back then, you'd be mocked mercilessly if your work lacked compositional discipline.

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: Oh how I miss those days! You know, it was a place where one could live and breathe art. It was a place of such brilliance, where a genius could find kindred spirits, unlike where we are now... *Sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: But I digress. Allow me to tell you about the absolute farce of an order I received.

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: It's an order for sculptures from the art exhibition in Snezhnograd. Open up the illustration and look for yourself — look at all those ill-disciplined designs! Look at how out of balance and harmony they all are!

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: Look at how everything is tilted, every line drawn in a fit of emotion! The very language of these sculptures is nothing more than a clumsy imitation of nature, a poor attempt at concealing the gross failure in structural ethics and moral principles of ice sculpture!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... What is she saying? Paimon doesn't understand a thing...

choices.text: Please don't ever talk like that, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't even if she tried!

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: That's alright, you don't have to feel bad for your lack of understanding. After all, not everyone has the means to pursue further studies in Snezhnograd or has the opportunity to rub shoulders with important people in the art world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What in the... She seems a little smug even, doesn't she???

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Me? Of course! Mind you, the townsfolk call me, Yarina, "the Master of the future", so I have very good reason to be! And I naturally have very good reason to discuss such matters at a level befitting a true master too.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Anyway! Since the two of you are so sincere and seem to know your place, I'm happy to explain this to you.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Every year, the folks at the Prime Ice sculpture exhibition in Snezhnograd would send their jobs here in Svetloledovka. And this year is no exception.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: And this time, they're planning a special themed exhibition called "Classics, Redux: The Glaciafruit Master Returns (A Special Homage Exhibition)."

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: That is to say, we Prime Ice designers are tasked with creating reproductions of that... that Glaciafruit artist. By the name of... Larionov or something.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: But how terribly disappointing! You'll know why once you look at the job order. None of those "works" are even really symmetrical! Even if they look balanced at first glance, a closer examination will tell you that the number of Prime Ice blocks needed on each side is totally different.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Is this "The Master" we're talking about? If you ask me, either this man lacks the proper technical foundation, or he's simply the tragic product of his times. He simply does not understand that compositional discipline is the eternal yardstick by which all Prime Ice works should be measured!

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: It's a good thing they sent the order to me. As a creator who has undergone artistic training in Snezhnograd, I have all along held myself to the standards of a Master.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: And because of that, I cannot allow my... the good name of Prime Ice sculpture to be sullied, not even in the slightest.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And so...?

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: So, I have corrected all the parts of that Larionov's works that had strayed from the morality of order, and have restored to them the necessary rigor and axial structural ethics.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There she goes again with that gobbledygook!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What she means to say is, she's turned all the designs symmetrical.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Is she even allowed to do that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why does Paimon get the feeling that... this is all about what she thinks "art" should be?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is the first time Paimon's even heard the term "compositional discipline" here in Snezhnaya. After all this time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Probably because it's an idea that's already outdated.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Ha! Hold on, I can't help but find the way you two are speaking rather offensive.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Neither of you has actually gone to art school in Snezhnograd, have you??? Just how much do you even know about what goes on in Snezhnograd's art world!?

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: If you are going to pooh-pooh my philosophy, at the very least, you should... you should first prove to me that you know what "compositional discipline" actually means!

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: You simply have no idea what it is that I'm working so hard towards! *Sigh* Well, it so happens that... I have an order that hasn't been fulfilled yet right here.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Fine. Let's have a wager! Show me that you can apply compositional discipline to the work, and I'll gladly admit defeat. As for the stake... Hmm. I'll stake half of the job payment on this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whoa, looks like someone got mad... Are we gonna take her up on the bet, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, we are talking about a good half of the job payment here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh heh, got it! Then let's show her what we've got!

choices.text: I don't understand a thing either.

dialogues.speaker: Malevich
dialogues.text: Wow... I can't believe it! This looks exactly like The Master's work! You've been such a great help. Here's a little something from me...

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: Ah, wonderful. I see that you have completed the "work of art." Here is your payment.

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: There are other designers around town who are probably also mired in "art-making" right now. If you want to earn more pocket change, you should take a walk around.

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: What...? So the two of you... do understand what compositional discipline is after all!

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: Fine. I'm a woman of my word. Looks like I'm not the only one worthy of the title of Master here in Svetloledovka...

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: Ah, wonderful. I see that you have completed the "work of art." Here is your payment.

dialogues.speaker: Malevich
dialogues.text: ...The road to becoming a Master is a long and arduous one indeed. Oh.. it's you. Have you thought of a way yet?

choices.text: I'd like to take a look at that job order again.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: The order is right there on the wooden board. You can take a look at it anytime.

choices.text: Let me think about it more.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Thanks, I'm counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: Art or a full belly? That has never been the question. Oh, it's the two of you. Any ideas how to proceed with this "work of art"?

choices.text: I'd like to take a look at the illustration on the job order again.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: It's right there on the plaque. Take a look whenever you like.

choices.text: Let me think about it again.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Malevich
dialogues.text: Wow... I can't believe it! This looks exactly like The Master's work! You've been such a great help. Here's a little something from me...

dialogues.speaker: Malevich
dialogues.text: There are other designers here who are also having trouble with their orders. So if you have some time to spare, you might want to take a walk around town...

dialogues.speaker: Malevich
dialogues.text: I'm now one step closer to becoming a Master, aren't I... Oh, it's you! What can I do for you?

choices.text: Tell me more about that "Master" you mentioned earlier.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: The Master Kazimir Larionov? Oh, he's the pride of Svetloledovka. He was an ordinary laborer who worked at the ice quarry, a nobody who never had any formal training in art...

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: But art has never been about one's background. They say his career began when he finally lost patience with the um... how do you say it... I think it was the "lack of artistic merit" he saw in the Prime Ice works around him...

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: So anyway, according to the papers, one day, after a spirited drinking session, The Master went around town and turned all the Prime Ice sculptures into Glaciafruit sculptures.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: "With their bold technique and the deliberate rejection of detail, these works marked a major departure from the realism that had dominated traditional Prime Ice sculpture at the time. And upon their delivery to Snezhnograd, they became an unprecedented sensation across the mainstream art world of the time..."

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: "A true Pioneer!" "A true work of Nature itself, just like the Glaciafruit!" "The man who has completely recast the relationship between the language of Prime Ice art and reality itself!"

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Ah, those are reviews... that I read in the papers. I don't really understand what they're saying, but I suppose they're all good things.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: If one day someone wrote that way about me, it'd mean that I've succeeded. So, I must continue to work hard to become an artist known all over Snezhnaya, just like the Master...

choices.text: About that Prime Ice art exhibition that's being held in Snezhnograd...

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Oh... That is an event organized by the Snezhnograd Veche. It's a real important event.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: It is also an incredible opportunity for Prime Ice designers like me. We create works based on the orders sent to us by the organizers, and these works are then shown at the exhibition... where they will be seen by many people.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: Although I haven't yet a chance to visit Snezhnograd myself, I can feel my heart burn as strongly as Kresnik's Torch whenever I think about how my work might actually be seen by the art world this time...

choices.text: Never mind.

response.speaker: Malevich
response.text: You take care, now!

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: Why, are you shying away from the wager?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Of course not.

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: Then I look forward to seeing your handiwork.

dialogues.speaker: Zarkaya
dialogues.text: Art or a full belly? Why is that even a question? Oh, it's you. What can I do for you?

choices.text: Tell me about your work...

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: I am a Prime Ice designer. Sometimes, people call me a "Prime Ice sculptor" too.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: But, if we're being honest, all people like us really do is process the fruits of the ice miners' labor. We dress it up, put a nice little bow on it here and there, and there you have it: a product.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: And if we're still being honest, this is one of the most ordinary jobs here in Svetloledovka. The way I see it, at least.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: But because our work involves this whole business of craft and handiwork with a bit of design added on top, at some point someone simply decided to call it "artistic creation."

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: And once something has been packaged into Art, everyone becomes real excited about it. Then throw in a few concepts, theories, and the right buzzwords...

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: Ah, the people of Snezhnograd, they're real suckers for this sort of thing.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: Of course, it's not something that really bothers me, as long as it means that I get paid more. And most importantly: as long as they don't come to me calling me an "artist."

choices.text: Tell me more about that "Master" exhibition.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: Is that something you're interested in? You should be able to find a blurb or two about it in the papers. Just ignore all those fawning articles about the municipal governme——

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: No, you can't do that. There'll be nothing left in the papers to read then. Never mind. I'll just tell you about it then.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: In short, this was the brainchild of someone in the Snezhnograd Veche. The purpose of this exhibition is to "enrich the spiritual life of the citizens" and, naturally, to boost tourism.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: This time, they're running a special edition titled "Classics, Redux: The Glaciafruit Master Returns (A Special Homage Exhibition)." Which really means, they're showing reproductions of some of the Master's works.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: You may ask, why would anyone be interested in an exhibition full of nothing but reproductions? But you have to understand where the bigwigs at the Veche are coming from.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: The idea, so it goes, is to give the common folk a chance to experience for themselves the illuminating force of Art through these reproductions. So, in their eyes, they're doing the people a real big favor with his.

choices.text: About "The Master"...

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: Are you talking about the "Glaciafruit Master"?

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: He's a sculptor by the name of Larionov. Although some people, Malevich included, are very eager to claim that he is some kind of peasant genius from this town, I'm not quite sure myself. My guess is that the whole story is simply a work of fiction.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: As far as I know, we've never had any Larionovs in this town. Not a single one.

choices.text: Never mind.

response.speaker: Zarkaya
response.text: See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: What...? So the two of you... do understand what compositional discipline is after all!

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: Fine. I'm a woman of my word. Looks like I'm not the only one worthy of the title of Master here in Svetloledovka...

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: I say, it would do well for the other designers in town to learn from you a little. Either they're into blind imitation, or they don't care about art at all. A good number of them have trouble making delivery on their orders, even...

dialogues.speaker: Yarina
dialogues.text: Art without discipline cannot be called art... Oh, it's you two again. Is there anything else I can do for you?

choices.text: Why do they call you the "the Master of the future"?

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Well... I can't be sure now. All the other designers in town just started calling me that one day.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: I suppose it's because it's clear that I'm a cut above the other designers here in terms of both taste and technique. Because I actually went to art school in Snezhnograd?

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: I've also given folks a helping hand here and there. Take that Malevich fellow, for example. I've already told him a long time ago blind imitation is not the way to go if he wants to break into the Snezhnayan art world. But he just doesn't get it.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: And then there's Zarkaya. While she actually has some potential, she never had the chance to study in Snezhnograd, and it shows in the kind of jobs she accepts. I've told her so many times to focus on the art-related jobs.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: You know, no one could have given this sort of precious advice here in Svetloledovka in the past!

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: As to why "future"... Anyhow, everyone says that it's only a matter of time before I make it big in Snezhnaya!

choices.text: Tell me more about that art exhibition happening in Snezhnograd...

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: To be completely frank with you, this exhibition has completely strayed from its original vision. What was meant to be a grand gathering of artistic treasures has now become nothing more than a collection of insipid, mediocre works!

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Ever since I left Snezhnograd, the vision and taste of the art world have been in steady decline year after year. Alas, this year they've even come up with some theme about reproducing the works of The Master...

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: They call it "a homage to the classics." Imagine my horror when I took my first look at that job order, and realized it was nothing but one passé work after another!

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: You must understand, the reason a work of art becomes a classic is because such works are able to, by their very nature, transcend the ages and stir the hearts of mankind no matter the generation or era.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: This so-called Master Larionov, or whoever he is, understands nothing of the aesthetics of discipline! And yet, one is forced to ask, how on earth have his works endured for so long?

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: If you ask me, he is far more likely than not a myth concocted by someone with absolutely no understanding of art, a feel-good story fabricated for the laymen.

choices.text: About "The Master"...

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: "The Master," Larionov? Just hearing that name makes my blood boil! His works completely lack compositional discipline. I have no idea why anyone would call him a "Master."

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: I must tell you, I'd never heard of that name when I was studying in Snezhnograd.

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: Does this "Prime Ice sculptor" even exist at all? I am now inclined to think it is nothing more than a fabrication, perhaps invented by some third-rate designer who cannot even sell their own work on their own terms...

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: These crude works, all paraded into the public eye in the name of "art," have, over time, inflated that name into fame and renown. And of course, in recent years, the Prime Ice art circle has conveniently failed to produce a single true master...

response.speaker: Yarina
response.text: "The Master," my foot! This is nothing more than a vulgar money grab!
